why: Quote verified verbatim (structured-outputs.md line 397, whole line read; the third sentence reinforces rather than reverses: 'The example below treats a result as successful only when the subtype is success and structured_output is present, and handles every other result as a failure'). The cited code line is real: event-adapter.ts:613-615 does spread {} when subtype==='success' and structured_output is undefined. But the CONSEQUENCE is false — this is the repo's recurring 'enforcement one layer up' false positive. The doc's rule is a rule for the CALLER that supplied the schema, and in this fork that caller is the CLI, which knows: apps/cli/src/index.ts:463 `const structuredMode = outputSchema !== undefined && !streamJson`, and the complete handler at :517-532 implements the doc's three branches exactly — success+present prints the value, error_max_structured_output_retries prints the errors and exits 1, and the final else emits the doc example's literal string 'Run ended without a structured output' and sets exitCode=1. So a schema-bearing Claude turn that ends success with no structured_output is surfaced as a failure, not a clean completion. Positive control run (temp copy of apps/cli/src/run.test.ts with the exhaustion fixture replaced by a bare `{ type: 'complete' }` — byte-identical to what the Claude adapter emits in the disputed case): `bun test -t 'sendAndStream exits non-zero'` printed `Error: Run ended without a structured output` and passed with exitCode 1; temp file deleted. The decision is also recorded, not accidental: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-structured-output.md:102 — 'success-without-output exits 1 (the docs' example branches)'. Sibling-subsystem note: the Pi backend implements structured output itself (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3481-3482 synthesizes structuredOutputErrors=['run completed without a structured output'] and always stamps structuredOutputSubtype), so its event is self-describing; the Claude backend delegates to the SDK and lets the schema-supplying caller decide. Both reach the same doc-mandated outcome. No non-schema-supplying consumer exists — grep -a across apps/electron, packages/ui, apps/webui, apps/viewer finds zero readers of structuredOutput*; SessionManager.ts:16982-16990 only forwards. Not in inert-worklist section 3, and not a branding/subscription product difference — refuted on the consequence.
correctedState: event-adapter.ts:613-615 does emit a bare complete event for a schema-bearing Claude turn that ends subtype 'success' with no structured_output, but the doc's requirement is met one layer up: the only consumer is the CLI, which set the schema itself (apps/cli/src/index.ts:463 structuredMode) and whose complete handler (:517-532) routes that exact event to the doc example's own failure branch — stderr 'Run ended without a structured output', exit 1 (verified by positive control). The residual, non-doc difference is cosmetic and internal: the Pi backend always stamps structuredOutputSubtype so its agent_end is self-describing, while the Claude path relies on caller knowledge. Adding an explicit subtype on the Claude side would be a consistency nicety, not a documented-contract fix.
